one_month_reasoning: No Adobe-scheduled event falls inside 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-30: Q3 FY26 results were already reported on Sep 10 (beat, Q4 revenue guide slightly below consensus, RPO +8%, CEO transition to Anil Chakravarthy effective Dec 1), Q4 FY26 results come in mid-December, and Adobe MAX is Nov 10-12, both outside the window. Figma's Q3 print is expected early November, also likely outside. In-window drivers are sector flows (software/AI-disruption rotation, which moved ADBE +/-4% days in September) and big-tech October earnings (Microsoft/Alphabet/Meta AI commentary) that can move the software group. With no specific catalyst I use a near-symmetric lognormal centred at ~$239 (tiny positive drift) with monthly vol ~11.7% (41%/3.5), slightly fattened tails.

fair_value.method: Blend of 9.5x forward P/E on NTM EPS of ~$28.6 as of Sep 2027 ($272, 60%) and a 10% FCF yield on FY27E FCF/share of ~$28 ($280, 40%), giving ~$275.

inputs_detail.derivation: FY26 $24.5 x (1 + ~7-8% revenue growth incl. Semrush annualisation, organic ARR growing ~9% but decelerating, + ~3-4% buyback share-count reduction, minus ~1pt from AI COGS gross-margin pressure) = ~+10%; slightly below consensus given 11 straight quarters of ARR deceleration.

ADBE trades ~8.7x FY27 consensus today and ~10x forward at its 5-yr low; Salesforce ~14.5x; software group ~22x. Adobe gets a discount to CRM because design-tool competitors (Figma +48%, Canva ~$4B ARR) are taking the growth pool; I allow slight re-rating from current depressed level, not a return to peer average.
FY26 OCF annualised ~$10.2B, +6% growth, minus ~$0.2B capex = ~$10.6-10.8B over ~385M avg shares.
Current yield ~11% at $238; peers in the de-rated software group trade at ~6-8%; 10% reflects a persistent AI-disruption discount with modest relief.

bear.story: Value-chain evidence keeps pointing against Adobe: Canva/Figma and model vendors (OpenAI images, Canva inside ChatGPT) take the growth pool, organic ARR decelerates to ~5-6%, freemium cannibalises Creative Cloud seat pricing, AI COGS keeps compressing gross margin, and the new CEO resets FY27 guidance. ~6.5x on ~$25.5 EPS.

base.story: Organic ARR growth drifts to ~8%, Semrush and GenStudio/CX Enterprise (with all five agency holding companies integrated) support the enterprise side, buybacks of ~$9B/yr shrink the share count 3-4%, EPS ~$27 in FY27; multiple stays depressed near 9x NTM EPS of ~$28.6.

bull.story: Firefly/AI-first ARR (>$650M, +150%) and 100M freemium MAU convert, ARR stabilises at ~10% organic, Canva's cost-driven growth cut and Figma's deceleration ease competitive fears, and software rotates back in; ~12x on ~$29.5 NTM EPS.

thesis_break_reason: At ~$170 ADBE would trade ~6.3x FY27 consensus EPS and a ~16% FCF yield. With net cash roughly neutral and a massive buyback, that level would most likely mean earnings expectations themselves are being cut (organic ARR growth falling toward low single digits, a FY27 guide well below $26 EPS from the new CEO, or evidence of seat losses to Canva/Figma/AI-native tools) rather than ordinary multiple volatility; it is also below the 52-week low of $190.

reasoning: Industry lane. Basic facts come from Adobe's Q3 FY26 release and 10-Q: revenue $6.76B +13% (flattered by Semrush, bought for $1.87B in April), ARR $27.5B +11.2%, but organic ~9.3%, RPO only +8%, FY26 EPS guide $24.45-24.50, and ~395M diluted shares shrinking ~1.8% per quarter. The value chain mostly argues that Adobe is losing share of the growth pool, not that its demand is collapsing. Figma grew 48% in Q2 with NDR of 136% and raised FY26 guidance to ~$1.465B. Canva has ~$4B ARR and 265M MAU, sits inside ChatGPT and targets a 2027 IPO. There are two offsets. Canva cut its growth forecast to ~20% because of AI serving costs, so competitors face the same AI cost squeeze Adobe does. And every major agency holding company (WPP, Omnicom, Publicis, Dentsu, Havas) is wired into Adobe's GenStudio/CX Enterprise, which supports the enterprise side. Stock-content peers (Getty/Shutterstock) are shifting to AI data licensing, which confirms that generic creative assets are being commoditised. Sector context: software has de-rated hard (IGV about -26% YTD, ADBE about 10x forward at a 5-yr low, CRM about 14.5x). Sell-side targets average about $268 (range $195-373). I value ADBE at ~$275 (9.5x NTM EPS $28.6 and a 10% FCF yield) but centre the distribution lower, at a median of ~$250. Two reasons: the de-rating trend is persistent (the stock returned -35% over the year despite EPS growth), and a CEO change adds guidance-reset risk. Scenarios are 25/50/25 at $165/$258/$350, a mean of about $259. The ladder is a lognormal with median $250 and sigma ~0.38, slightly below the 41% realized vol because the 12-month outcome is anchored by ~10x earnings and a large buyback, with modestly fattened lower tails. Research limits: Twelve Data estimates/targets needed a paid plan and Alpha Vantage was rate-limited, so consensus EPS and targets come from web press summaries; direct sec.gov curl returned empty, so the 10-Q was read via web fetch; X/Twitter was not attempted.
